approachQuestion.prompt:
Free links and paid links. In a directed network, each edge costs either 0 or 1 credit. Given s and t, return the minimum total credits for a directed walk from s to t, or -1 if unreachable. A zero-edge walk from s to itself costs zero. Zero-cost cycles are legal.

Input: read-only outgoing lists of (neighbor,cost), vertex IDs 0..V-1; 1 <= V <= 200000, 0 <= E <= 400000. No duplicate ordered edges; self-loops are permitted. Every cost is exactly 0 or 1. Optimize worst-case running time; there is no tie-break on which minimum-cost walk is chosen. Output only the cost.

Example: edges=[(0,1,1),(0,2,0),(2,1,0)], s=0,t=1, output=0, via 0->2->1.

options.text: Use tentative distances and a deque of (vertex,distanceSnapshot). Start s at zero. Pop from the front, skip stale or finalized entries, and finalize the vertex. For every improving relaxation, put the new entry at the front for a zero-cost edge or at the back for a one-cost edge.
options.feedback: The deque keeps current tentative distance layers in order because an improvement from distance d has distance d or d+1. Finalizing the next current entry is safe, including across zero-cost cycles.

options.text: Run Dijkstra with a binary min-heap of tentative distances and skip outdated heap entries.
options.feedback: Nonnegative weights make Dijkstra correct for the entire domain. But maintaining a general priority heap adds removable ordering work when the only increments are zero and one.

options.text: Run ordinary vertex BFS, permanently accept each first discovery and sum the edge costs along that discovery route.
options.feedback: In the example, the direct edge may discover 1 with cost 1 before the two-edge route reaches it for zero credits. Fewest edges and least cost are different objectives.

options.text: Use a deque but put every discovered entry at the front, and permanently finalize each vertex when first popped without comparing tentative distance priorities.
options.feedback: For ordered edges 0->1 cost 0, 0->2 cost 1, 1->2 cost 0, pushing both at the front pops 2 at cost 1 before 1. Finalizing it there misses the zero-credit route 0->1->2.

feedback.reason: Unit-cost BFS layering generalizes to two adjacent cost layers when each edge adds either zero or one; a vertex must not be permanently fixed merely on discovery.
details: Initialize distances to infinity and finalized to false; set s to zero and push (s,0) into a deque. Pop the front entry. Skip it if finalized or if its snapshot differs from the current distance. Otherwise finalize the vertex and scan its outgoing edges. If distance[u]+cost improves an unfinalized neighbor, update its distance and push a snapshot entry to the front for cost zero or back for cost one. Continue until empty; return the target distance or -1.

Zero-cost improvements go to the deque front and unit-cost improvements to the back. Snapshot/finalized checks discard stale entries before scanning edges. Ordinary FIFO would not preserve increasing weighted distance.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze zero-one-deque. V counts vertices and E directed edges. Use V-entry distance/finalized arrays and a preallocated circular deque of 2V fixed-size snapshot entries with constant-time front/back operations. Distances are nonnegative machine integers or an infinity sentinel. There is no hashing, recursion, input copying, shifting, or amortized growth. Include stale-entry processing and array initialization. Exclude input and scalar result; include arrays and deque. Explain why 2V slots suffice under the zero/one domain.
constraints: Choose the tightest standard worst-case bound for the specified implementation.

options.text: O(V + E) time, O(V) auxiliary space
O((V + E) log V) time, O(V) auxiliary space
O(V + E) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Finalize each vertex once and scan its outgoing edges once using a 0-1 deque.
details: The option “O(V + E) time, O(V) auxiliary space” is tight: current deque snapshots are processed in nondecreasing distance order. When first discovered from a current distance d, a vertex receives d or d+1; before finalization it can only improve once, from d+1 to d. Thus each vertex has at most two inserted snapshots, so 2V deque slots suffice and stale pops total O(V). Each finalized vertex scans its outgoing edges once, giving O(V+E) time including initialization. Arrays and deque occupy O(V). The option “O((V + E) log V) time, O(V) auxiliary space” adds an unused heap factor. The option “O(V + E) time, O(1) auxiliary space” drops working storage. The option “O(VE) time, O(V) auxiliary space” charges repeated edge scans even though only the single finalization scans a vertex’s list.
